title: Choose Mezzanine's visual world
question: The roll assigned House Lights. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: House Lights
options.lineage: 1920s–30s movie-palace mezzanine, seen at the moment the house lights go down
options.thesis: The app is the auditorium: chrome is house lighting that dims to nothing when the film starts.
options.viewport: Home seen from the balcony: the featured title fills a proscenium-framed 'screen' at the top, shelves step down below it like raked rows, the sidebar is the dark side aisle.
options.risk: Tips into theme-park kitsch if ornament goes beyond one plaster rule and the marquee board.

raised.raise: Nothing glides on the marquee: Up Next letters and the countdown change in discrete steps with one overshoot, like changeable letters on a track.
Every title carries a ruled programme caption naming each part: 1080p · HEVC · E-AC-3 5.1 · 17 subtitles.
One control reshapes the house: the density slider re-rakes every row in one continuous pull.
Total palette commitment: chrome uses only velvet, ivory and peacock; colour on screen belongs to the films.
Depth is chronology: Continue Watching stacks by recency, the newest pass in front.

options.label: Bias Light
options.lineage: a dark room lit only by the screen and the bias light behind it
options.thesis: Each film lights the room: Plex's four UltraBlur colours spill from the art across a near-black graphite ground.
options.viewport: The selected title's backdrop and clearLogo own the top; its four corner colours wash the whole window; shelves sit on graphite below.
options.risk: Familiar: close to where most media-app redesigns land (Apple TV, Infuse 8); the spill must stay subtle or it reads as glow-neon.

options.label: Cutting Bench
options.lineage: a film editor's bench: work print between pins, tape flag where you stopped
options.thesis: Your library as a select rail: every episode a punched frame, a folded tape flag marks where you stopped.
options.viewport: A perforated rail crosses Home at a fixed height carrying Continue Watching; set-aside titles hang on pins below.
options.case: Strong product clarity (flag = resume, pins = watchlist, grease cross = watched); weaker audience fit: the owner watches films, he doesn't cut them. Orange translated to splice-tape magenta to avoid Plex.
options.risk: A single-ink world may feel severe across a week of binges.

options.label: Depot Blind
options.thesis: Content as cloth courses stepping under one window.
options.viewport: One fixed window, rows stepping through it.
options.risk: Transit has nothing to do with watching films.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no audience link, and a single window hides the library.
options.kept: Discrete stepped motion with one overshoot, now on the marquee and Up Next countdown.

options.label: Sapeur Plate
options.thesis: Each title as a portrait plate with a ruled caption.
options.viewport: One figure per plate, caption below.
options.case: Fuses poorly: browsing hundreds of titles needs rows, not plates.
options.kept: The ruled caption naming every part, now under each title.

options.label: Indoor Sun
options.thesis: Everything flattened to one sodium amber.
options.risk: Amber kills the films' own colour.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a player must show colour truthfully.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Apple TV app / Infuse, executed impeccably: black ground, poster rows, glass sidebar, system blue.
canonCard.viewport: Hero backdrop carousel over shelves of posters.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from what you just left by design.
